epv.note: Price above EPV: the market pays for growth. EPV above tangible book: the business earns more than its assets would cost to rebuild — a sign of a moat (Greenwald). EPV below tangible book: the assets earn less than their cost.

implied_return.note: The yearly return a buyer at today's price earns if each model's assumptions hold (an implied cost of capital). Above the cost of equity: the price leaves room; below: the price already asks for more than the models deliver.

wacc.formula: WACC = wₑ × kₑ + w_d × k_d × (1 − t);  kₑ = r_f + β × ERP
steps: β (Blume-adjusted) = 0.67 × raw β 1.43 + 0.33 = 1.29  (104 weekly returns vs SPY, R² 0.10)
k_d = 6.40%  (5-year Treasury 4.91% + model spread 149 bp (bond-calibrated, app/debt.py)); after tax 6.40% × (1 − 0%) = 6.40%

methods.formula: FCFF = EBIT × (1 − t) + D&A − capex − ΔWC;  EV = Σ FCFF/(1+WACC)^t + TV/(1+WACC)^5;  TV = NOPAT₆ × (1 − g ÷ ROIC) ÷ (WACC − g);  value = (EV − debt + cash − claims) ÷ shares
steps: growth by year 21%, 18%, 14%, 10%, 6%; EBIT margin 14.8%; D&A 17.0% of revenue; capex 11.4% of revenue; ΔWC 10% of each revenue increase

methods.formula: EPV = adjusted earnings ÷ WACC − net debt;  adjusted earnings = normalized EBIT × (1 − t) + D&A − maintenance capex;  normalized EBIT = average margin × revenue

methods.formula: FCFE = net income − (1 − d) × (capex − D&A + ΔWC);  value = Σ FCFE ÷ (1 + kₑ)ᵗ + terminal ÷ (1 + kₑ)⁵;  terminal = net income₆ × (1 − g ÷ ROE) ÷ (kₑ − g)

methods.formula: Value = (assets in place + C − net debt) ÷ shares;  C = S·N(d₁) − K·e^(−rT)·N(d₂), d₁ = [ln(S ÷ K) + (r + σ²/2)T] ÷ σ√T, d₂ = d₁ − σ√T
steps: S = the expansion in year 5: the revenue it adds $911.9M (to $1.92B) × margin 14.8% × (1 − tax), as a growing perpetuity, discounted = $851.0M
K = capital to build it: $911.9M ÷ sales-to-capital 0.93 = $978.3M
σ = 83% (its stock, a year of daily closes), T = 5 years, r = 4.91% → C = $563.7M
assets in place = NOPAT $149.7M ÷ WACC = $1.40B; value = ($1.40B + $563.7M − net debt $154.0M) ÷ 126,548,000 = $14.33
